# Galaxy Tool Submission

Use this skill after the scientific tool and parameters have been selected. Build
complex inputs from the selected wrapper's live schema and verify the created job
resolved the intended objects.

## Dataset Inputs

- Wait for uploaded data to reach `ok` with the expected datatype before using
  the final history dataset ID.
- Verify paired mates use distinct dataset IDs and preserve forward/reverse
  order.
- For reference-source conditionals, confirm the job resolved the intended
  history reference or built-in genome rather than a default branch.

## Nested And Repeated Payloads

- Use input format `21.01` for natural nested JSON, repeat lists, and conditional
  objects. Use legacy format onl

    def copy_history(self, history_id: str, name: str | None = None, all_datasets: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Create a new history by copying an existing one.

        :type history_id: str
        :param history_id: ID of the history to copy.

        :type name: str
        :param name: Optional name for new history

        :type all_datasets: bool
        :param all_datasets: Whether to copy also deleted datasets and dataset collections.

        :rtype: dict
        :return: Dictionary containing information about the newly created history
        """
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {"source": "history"}
        if name is not None:
            payload["name"] = name
        payload["history_id"] = history_id
        if all_datasets:
            payload["all_datasets"] = all_datasets

        return self._post(payload)

# Galaxy UDT Templates And Troubleshooting

Read only the section needed for the current UDT.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a pinned BioContainer found through one
bounded live BioContainers lookup. Use a bare tagged reference without
`docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  selected-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

For generated glue scripts, avoid nested `python -c` quoting. A base64 argument
keeps the script as one shell token:

```bash
SCRIPT_B64='BASE64_WITHOUT_NEWLINES'
python -c 'import base64, pathlib, sys; pathlib.Path("job.py").write_bytes(base64.b64decode(sys.argv[1]))' "$SCRIPT_B64"
python job.py "$(inputs.inpu

representation.name: Gene length versus immune-cell mean expression Pearson correlations
representation.shell_command:
set -eu
cat > analysis.R <<'RSCRIPT'
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly=TRUE)
if (length(args) != 3L) stop("Expected count matrix, gene metadata, and sample annotation")
counts_raw <- read.csv(args[1], check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
gene_meta <- read.csv(args[2], check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
sample_annot <- read.csv(args[3], check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

required_meta <- c("Geneid", "Length", "gene_biotype")
required_annot <- c("sample", "celltype")
if (!all(required_meta %in% names(gene_meta))) stop("Gene metadata lacks required columns")
if (!all(required_annot %in% names(sample_annot))) stop("Sample annotation lacks required columns")
if (ncol(counts_raw) < 2L) stop("Count matrix has no sample columns")

count_gene_ids <- as.character(counts_raw[[1]])
meta_gene_ids <- as.character(gene_meta$Geneid)
if (anyDuplicated(count_gene_ids)) stop("Duplicate gene identifiers in count matrix")
if (anyDuplicated(meta_gene_ids)) stop("Duplicate Geneid values in gene metadata")
meta_idx <- match(count_gene_ids, meta_gene_ids)
if (anyNA(meta_idx)) stop("Not all count-matrix genes were found in gene metadata")

sample_names <- colnames(counts_raw)[-1]
if (anyDuplicated(sample_names)) stop("Duplicate sample columns in count matrix")
if (anyDuplicated(sample_annot$sample)) stop("Duplicate sample identifiers in annotation")
if (!all(sample_annot$sample %in% sample_names)) stop("Not all annotated samples were found in count matrix")

protein <- gene_meta$gene_biotype[meta_idx] == "protein_coding"
lengths <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gene_meta$Length[meta_idx][protein]))
expr <- as.matrix(counts_raw[protein, -1, drop=FALSE])
storage.mode(expr) <- "double"

celltypes <- c("CD4", "CD8", "CD14", "CD19")
correlations <- numeric(length(celltypes))
n_samples <- integer(length(celltypes))
n_genes <- integer(length(celltypes))
for (i in seq_along(celltypes)) {
  samples <- as.character(sample_annot$sample[sample_annot$celltype == celltypes[i]])
  if (length(samples) == 0L) stop(paste("No samples for", celltypes[i]))
  if (!all(samples %in% colnames(expr))) stop(paste("Missing count columns for", celltypes[i]))
  avg_expression <- rowMeans(expr[, samples, drop=FALSE], na.rm=FALSE)
  keep <- is.finite(lengths) & is.finite(avg_expression)
  if (sum(keep) < 3L) stop(paste("Too few finite protein-coding genes for", celltypes[i]))
  correlations[i] <- cor(lengths[keep], avg_expression[keep], method="pearson")
  n_samples[i] <- length(samples)
  n_genes[i] <- sum(keep)
}
summary <- data.frame(
  celltype=celltypes,
  n_samples=n_samples,
  n_protein_coding_genes=n_genes,
  pearson_correlation=correlations,
  absolute_correlation=abs(correlations),
  method=rep("Pearson", length(celltypes)),
  gene_scope=rep("protein_coding", length(celltypes)),
  stringsAsFactors=FALSE
)
write.table(summary, file="correlations.tsv", sep="	", quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE, col.names=TRUE, digits=17)
winner <- celltypes[which.min(abs(correlations))]
writeLines(winner, con="answer.txt")
RSCRIPT
Rscript analysis.R "$(inputs.counts.path)" "$(inputs.gene_meta.path)" "$(inputs.sample_annot.path)"
